claim: Moselsteig Stage 8 (Leiwen – Neumagen-Dhron) is a vineyard-and-rock-cliff stage ending in Germany's oldest wine town at the Stella Noviomagi Roman ship replica.
quote: On this unique stage between Leiwen and Neumagen-Dhron you walk through idyllic vineyards and past wild rock cliffs. The path ends in Neumagen-Dhron, the oldest wine town in Germany, at the dock of the 'Stella Noviomagi'

claim: Moselsteig Stage 8 Leiwen–Neumagen-Dhron is 14.09 km; Stage 9 Neumagen-Dhron–Kesten 17.97 km; Stage 10 Kesten–Bernkastel-Kues 14.69 km; Stage 11 Bernkastel-Kues–Ürzig 16.99 km; Stage 7 Mehring–Leiwen 14.50 km; Stage 6 Schweich–Mehring 12.38 km.
quote: 5 Trier – Schweich 19.91 km | 6 Schweich – Mehring 12.38 km | 7 Mehring – Leiwen 14.50 km | 8 Leiwen – Neumagen-Dhron 14.09 km | 9 Neumagen-Dhron – Kesten/Osann-Monzel 17.97 km | 10 Kesten/Osann-Monzel – Bernkastel-Kues 14.69 km | 11 Bernkastel-Kues – Ürzig 16.99 km

claim: Moselsteig Stage 11 (Bernkastel-Kues – Ürzig) is roughly 16.7 km with ~684 m elevation gain, rated difficult and takes 5.5-6 hours.
quote: The trail is 16.7 km long... elevation gain is 684 m... considered a difficult/hard hike... takes an average of 5.5–6 hours

claim: The Calmont Klettersteig between Bremm and Ediger-Eller is 3.54 km, ~1.5 h, +186 m / -210 m, medium difficulty, traversing Europe's steepest vineyard with ladders, steel cables and rock-ridge sections — but it lies ~40-50 km drive from Piesport (28.7 km straight line), at the outer edge of a day-trip radius.
quote: Distance: 3.54 km - Duration: Approximately 1.5 hours - Elevation gain: 186 m - Elevation loss: 210 m - Difficulty: Medium... constructed in 2002... steel cables, ladders, as well as numerous steps and pegs

claim: The Calmont rises 380 m between Bremm and Ediger-Eller with up to 65° incline (Europe's steepest vineyard) and is secured with 6 ladders, ~100 m of safety rope, 22 step irons and 16 grip pegs; sure-footedness and freedom from dizziness required but no via-ferrata kit needed.
quote: Between Bremm and Ediger-Eller it rises 380 meters high... an incline of up to 65 degrees, it is Europe's steepest vineyard... 6 ladders are installed, approximately 100 meters of safety ropes, 22 step irons and 16 grip pegs

claim: The Piesporter Moselbogen 'Leuchtpunkt' circular hike is 7.98 km, ~2 h 15 min, easy, with 105 m ascent / 205 m descent, running through the Goldtröpfchen vineyard past the St. Michael church and a Roman wine press, starting at the Bürgerhaus Piesport.
quote: approximately 7.98 kilometers and takes around 2 hours and 15 minutes... Rated as easy... 105 meters of ascent and 205 meters of descent... distinctive amphitheater-like Mosel bend

claim: The Zummethöhe panorama between Leiwen and Trittenheim was voted 'Best of the Vineyard Views – Moselle' in 2016 and is reached from a car park where the Kronenberg and Sonnenberg circular trails join to form a 15 km loop.
quote: voted 'Best of the Vineyard Views - Moselle' in 2016... Kronenberg circular (downstream direction) and Sonnenberg circular (upstream direction) meet at the Zummethöhe car park to form a 15 km-long trail

claim: The Fünf-Seen-Blick is a freely accessible 23 m wooden tower in the forest between Detzem and Mehring, with 105 steps to the top platform giving views from Schweich to Klüsserath and into the Eifel; it sits directly on Moselsteig Stage 7.
quote: 23 meter high wooden tower located about 25 kilometers from Trier... Climbing the 105 steps to the upper platform... grand view over the Moselle valley from Schweich to Klüsserath and far into the Eifel... directly on the Stefan-Andres hiking trail and on Moselsteig trail stage 07

claim: The Seitensprung Mehringer Schweiz partner-trail loop covers ~13.7 km with ~575 m of climbing, takes 4.5-5 hours, and includes the Fünf-Seen-Blick tower plus the Triolago recreation lake and Roman Villa Mehring.
quote: covers 8.5 miles (approximately 13.7 km), with an elevation gain of 1,886 feet (approximately 575 meters) and takes about 4.5–5 hours... 20-metre high wooden viewing tower... 'Five Moselle lakes'

claim: The Römersteig premium trail runs 22.26 km one-way from Hinkelstein near Trittenheim to Minheim, with +435 m / -300 m, rated difficult, crossing the Mosel twice and passing slate caves, Roman archaeological sites and a reconstructed wine press at Piesport.
quote: spans '22,26 km' and takes approximately '6 hours 20 minutes'... features '435 m' of ascent and '300 m' of descent... Rated as 'difficult'... begins 'at Hinkelstein bei 54349 Trittenheim' and concludes 'in 54518 Minheim'

claim: Moselsteig Stage 7 (Mehring – Leiwen) climbs through fir/spruce forest and beech high-forest in the Mehringer Schweiz and features a 20 m wooden viewing tower over the 'Five Moselle lakes' bends.
quote: challenging stage leads through the woodland around Mehringer Schweiz... steep paths through fir and spruce forests, through a high-level beech forest... 20-metre high wooden viewing tower... 'Five Moselle lakes'

claim: The Panorama-Wanderweg Piesport is a ~5 km loop starting and ending at the Piesporter Heiligenhäuschen car park, leading to the Weislei shelter and the 'Großer Moselblick' viewpoint that gives a 180° panorama over Piesport, Minheim and Neumagen-Dhron.
quote: approximately 5 kilometers long... 180 degree panorama over the Moselle valley with the wine villages of Piesport, Minheim and Neumagen-Dhron... begins and ends at the 'Piesporter Heiligenhäuschen' car park

claim: Moselsteig Stage 7 from Mehring to Leiwen is a partner-stage of the Seitensprung Mehringer Schweiz and is considered one of the more demanding stages of the Moselsteig.
quote: Moselsteig Trail Stage 07: Mehring – Leiwen

claim: The Saar-Hunsrück region holds 112 Traumschleifen (premium circular loops) of 6-20 km and 24 shorter Traumschleifchen up to 7 km, certified by the German Hiking Institute and themed individually.
quote: 112 Traumschleifen (dream loops) and 24 Traumschleifchen... between 6 and 20 km long, designed as circular routes... designed according to German Hiking Institute standards

claim: The Moselachter premium loop at Trittenheim is ~14 km (8.8 mi) with ~412 m (1,351 ft) climbing, rated moderate, 4-4.5 hours, with views into both the Mosel and Dhron valleys.
quote: Moselachter is a trail located in Trittenheim... covers 8.8 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,351 ft and takes about 4–4.5 hr to complete

claim: The Piesporter Goldtröpfchen vineyard slopes range from 30% to 70% gradient and recommended footwear is hiking/trekking shoes with provisions.
quote: vineyards have slopes ranging from 30 to 70 percent, with some being extremely steep... hiking or trekking shoes are recommended, as well as provisions in a backpack

claim: Weingut Reinhold Haart in Piesport (Ausoniusufer 18, +49 6507 2015) is run by Johannes and Theo Haart, farming nine hectares of Mosel steep slope including the Goldtröpfchen, with tastings by prior appointment.
quote: Today, this historic winery in Piesport, Mosel, is managed by Johannes and Marcus Haart, who oversee nine hectares of steep vineyards and dedicate themselves to producing top-quality rieslings.

claim: Weingut Fritz Haag in Brauneberg (Dusemonder Str. 44, +49 6534 410) farms 19.5 ha of Riesling including the Brauneberger Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr grand crus, with tastings pre-arranged by email at info@weingut-fritz-haag.de.
quote: The winery dates back to 1605, and has been run by Oliver Haag and his wife Jessica since the beginning of 2005. The vineyards cover 19.5 hectares of vines with slopes of up to 80%, with eight hectares in the top Brauneberg sites of Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr.

claim: Weingut Nik Weis - St. Urbans-Hof in Leiwen (Urbanusstraße 16, +49 6507 93770) offers bookable tastings of Rieslings from five VDP.Grosse Lage sites including a view over Laurentiuslay.
quote: At the winery, you can take a sensory walk through six of the best vineyards of the Moselle and Saar during a wine tasting and enjoy a wonderful view of the VDP.GROSSE LAGE® LAURENTIUSLAY.

claim: Weingut Markus Molitor's Haus Klosterberg vinothek in Bernkastel-Kues charges €20 per person to taste from a list of 40+ wines across 15 sites (Bernkastel, Graach, Wehlen, Zeltingen); appointment required by phone or email (vinothek@markusmolitor.com, +49 6532 954000).
quote: In the special atmosphere of the vinotheque at Klosterberg House... you can enjoy unique wine tastings, choosing your personal selection from more than 40 different wines... The list of wines to taste is €20 per person... appointments are kindly requested in advance.

claim: The St-Nikolaus-Hospital Vinothek in Bernkastel-Kues (Cusanusstr. 2) is the world's largest Mosel-Riesling vinothek, open daily 10:00-18:00 with walk-in tasting 10:00-17:00 at €30 per person spanning over 100 wines.
quote: Wine tasting is available daily between 10 am and 5 pm at 30,00 € per person... The vinotheque in Bernkastel-Kues is located in the vaulted cellars of St Nicholas Hospital and is the largest vinotheque for Moselle Riesling in the world.

claim: Weingut Willi Schaefer in Graach (Hauptstraße 130, +49 6531 8041) farms only 4.2 ha across Graacher Domprobst, Himmelreich and Wehlener Sonnenuhr; visits accepted only April–July by prior appointment, none August–March.
quote: Visits, within their possibilities, are from April to July by prior appointment. No tasting opportunities from August to March.

claim: Weingut Schloss Lieser (Thomas Haag), at Am Markt 1-5 in Lieser, runs a Vinothek/shop Mon-Tue/Thu-Fri 10:00-17:00 and Sat 11:00-15:00; full tastings require advance reservation by email and the estate does not offer cellar or vineyard tours.
quote: The wine shop is open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 10am to 5pm, and Saturday from 11am to 3pm... For a comprehensive wine tasting, advance reservation is required by email... tastings are tasting only and no guided tours of the vineyard or cellar can be offered.

claim: Weingut Selbach-Oster's Vinothek at Gänsfelderstraße 20 in Zeltingen-Rachtig opens Wed-Fri 11:00-17:00 with Mosel-side terraces overlooking Ürziger Würzgarten; six-wine guided tastings on request from €60 minimum, none during harvest until end of October.
quote: Wine tasting sessions include six wines, dry to sweet according to your choice, paired with traditional dishes and appetizers... Wine tastings are offered for smaller groups with a minimum of €60.00.

claim: Weingut Wwe. Dr. H. Thanisch (Erben Thanisch) in Bernkastel-Kues, owner of the legendary Berncasteler Doctor vineyard, opens Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00 and Sat 11:00-16:00; tastings only by prior registration (+49 6531 2282, info@thanisch-vdp.de).
quote: The winery is open Monday–Friday 10 am – 5 pm, Saturday 11 am – 4 pm or by appointment. Wine tastings are only conducted by prior registration by phone (+49 6531 2282) or email.

claim: Moselland eG winegrowers' cooperative Vinothek at Bornwiese 2, Bernkastel-Kues opens Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00 and Sat 09:00-12:00; group tastings on request require minimum 10 people (20 on weekends/holidays).
quote: Opening hours are Monday to Friday: 09:00 - 18:00 o'clock, Saturday: 09:00 - 12:00... Wine tastings are carried out on request. The minimum number of participants is 10 persons, on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays at least 20 persons.

claim: The Piesporter Moselbogen circular hike (~7 km) loops through the Goldtröpfchen steep-slope vineyard along the Mosel, marketed as a wine-and-nature 'Spotlight' trail right in Piesport.
quote: The approximately 7-kilometer circular hike runs in a bow shape through the famous vineyard 'Piesporter Goldtröpfchen' and along the Mosel riverbank.

claim: Walk-in wine venues in Piesport itself include Vinothek Piesport, Weinhaus Hoffmann and the cosy Weinbar am Markt, alongside producers Reinhold Haart, Julian Haart and Reuscher-Haart.
quote: Vinothek Piesport - Offers a wide selection of local wines for tasting and purchase. Weinhaus Hoffmann - Family-run establishment providing expert guidance on Mosel wines. Weinbar am Markt - Cozy wine bar with rotating selections from local producers.

claim: Weingut Clüsserath-Weiler in Trittenheim (Brückenstraße 9), run by Verena Clüsserath on 6.5 ha including Trittenheimer Apotheke, opens Mon-Fri 8:00-18:00 and weekends 8:00-13:00 for on-site tasting in the old barrel cellar.
quote: The winery is located at Brückenstraße 9, D-54349 Trittenheim, and is open Monday-Friday 8-18 Uhr and Saturday/Sunday 8-13 Uhr... Wines can be tasted on site in the old barrel cellar where the noble Clüsserath-Weiler wines mature.

claim: Weingut Schloss Lieser is recognized as a top Mosel VDP estate and one of Bernkastel-Kues region's flagship visitor wineries, set in Lieser village across the river from Brauneberg.
quote: Weingut Schloss Lieser

claim: Bernkastel tourism officially lists Weingut Markus Molitor's Haus Klosterberg as a visitor destination within the city of Bernkastel-Kues, around 15 km from Piesport.
quote: Winery Markus Molitor

claim: The Römische Kelteranlage at Piesport-Niederemmel is a reconstructed Roman wine press at Ausoniusufer 54498 Piesport, freely accessible under an open protective structure with mash and must tanks, press and smoke chamber, and is a station on the 'Roads of the Romans' route; an annual Roman wine press festival in early October presses grapes the Roman way.
quote: The Romans already made wine from the best vineyards of the Moselle ... faithfully restored and partially rebuilt with mash and must tanks, a wine press and a smoke chamber.

claim: The Stella Noviomagi in Neumagen-Dhron (about 6 km downstream from Piesport) is the largest seaworthy reconstructed Roman ship in the German-speaking world, 17.95 m long and 4.20 m wide; in 2026 it sails May 2–Oct 24 Sat 16:00–17:30, May 3–Oct 25 Sun 10:00–12:00 (wine-pressing cruises), and Wed 14:00–16:00 in July/Aug/Sep windows; full charter €500 for 32 pax.
quote: Saturdays 16:00–17:30 (Cultural cruises, May 2–October 24); Sundays 10:00–12:00 (Wine-pressing cruises, May 3–October 25) ... Full Charter (up to 32 passengers): €500

claim: Neumagen-Dhron is celebrated as the oldest wine village in Germany; the original wine-ship tomb sculpture (~220 AD) showing six rowers, two helmsmen, 22 oars and four wine barrels was excavated 1878 from the late-Roman fortress wall and now sits in the Rheinisches Landesmuseum Trier, with replicas displayed in Neumagen-Dhron.
quote: a large sculpture depicting a ship loaded with wine barrels was found in a prominent tomb of a Roman wine merchant from around 220 AD. The wine ship shows six rowers, two helmsmen and 22 oars

claim: Burg Landshut sits on a rocky ledge ~60 m above Bernkastel-Kues (about 17 km from Piesport), was built in 1276 atop a 4th–5th century Roman fort linked to Emperor Constantius I, and offers a barrier-free circular route plus panoramic Mosel views; reached by the Burg-Landshut-Express shuttle (Apr–Oct, hourly 11:00–17:00) or a steep 30-minute 750 m walk.
quote: The castle was constructed in 1276 and built upon a fort dating back to the 4th or 5th century ... stands atop a rocky ledge some 60 metres wide and overlooks Bernkastel.

claim: The Burg Landshut grounds and viewpoint are freely accessible; the on-site restaurant (in the rebuilt keep complex) opens daily 12:00–21:00 as of 2026, with only a small fee to climb the tower.
quote: Monday through Sunday from 12:00 pm to 9:00 pm

claim: The St-Nikolaus-Hospital / Cusanusstift in Kues was founded in 1465 by Nikolaus von Kues as a hospice for 33 elderly men; its Gothic chapel with winged Passion altar is free to enter (Sun–Fri 09:00–18:00, Sat 09:00–15:00) and its library — one of the world's most valuable private manuscript collections (9th–15th c.) — is only accessible on guided tours Tue 10:30 and Fri 15:00 from April to October.
quote: Chapel: Sunday–Friday 9:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.; Saturday 9:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. ... Library accessible only via guided tours ... Open tours April to October on Tuesdays at 10:30 AM and Fridays at 3:00 PM.

claim: The Moselweinmuseum at Cusanusstraße 2 in Kues opens daily 10:00–17:00 from 16 April to 31 October and 14:00–17:00 from 1 November to 15 April; the attached Vinothek in the vaulted cellars of the St-Nikolaus-Hospital offers ~140 Mosel-Saar-Ruwer wines to taste and buy.
quote: The museum is open daily from April 16 to October 31 from 10:00-17:00 and from November 1 to April 15 from 14:00-17:00 ... approximately 140 wines and sparkling wines from the Mosel-Saar-Ruwer wine region

claim: Bernkastel-Kues' medieval Marktplatz has a 400-year history with the Renaissance town hall, the 1416 Spitzhäuschen (the oldest and most photographed half-timbered building, narrow at the base and jettied wide above to dodge land taxes), the Heinz'sches Haus and St-Michaels-Brunnen, all within easy walking distance.
quote: The medieval market square has a 400-year history with impressive half-timbered houses. Notable features include the Renaissance town hall, the Spitzhäuschen (pointed house), the Heinz'sche House, and St. Michael's Fountain.

claim: The Spitzhäuschen was built in 1416 as a narrow-base, wide-top half-timbered house to minimise the land tax (charged on ground footprint) and houses a wine bar today; it is still open to the public.
quote: It was built in 1416, and was constructed as high and crooked as it is today because taxes had to be paid on building land. The base of the house is extremely narrow, with the upper floors jettied out wider

claim: Burg/Schloss Veldenz (about 9 km from Piesport, 1.5 km southeast of Veldenz village) was the largest castle on the Central Mosel in the 15th century, destroyed by French troops in 1681 and partly rebuilt; guided tours run every Wednesday at 15:00 from April through October for €8 per person, children up to 'sword length' free.
quote: The guided tour of Veldenz Castle takes place every Wednesday at 3.00 pm from April to October inclusive ... The price per person is 8 €, children up to sword length get free entry.

claim: The Roman Villa Rustica in Mehring (~25 km from Piesport, on the way to Trier) is a partly reconstructed Gallo-Roman estate of 48 × 29 m and 34 rooms with a hot/cold bath complex, heated mosaic-floored living room, two corner towers and porticus front, originally built 2nd–5th century AD; open year-round free of charge, with guided tours April–October Sundays 11:30.
quote: Open year-round, free to the public ... 48 by 29 meters and had 34 rooms ... hot and cold bath and a latrine, was originally built between the 2nd and 5th centuries AD ... Tours of the villa are available from April to October on Sundays at 11:30 a.m.

claim: The Roman Villa Urbana of Longuich (about 28 km from Piesport, just inside the 30 km radius) is the excavated remains of a luxurious Roman country retreat with its own baths; guided tours run May–October on Sundays at 10:30 (registration 06502-994111).
quote: Guided tours through the Roman Villa take place from May to October on Sundays at 10:30 AM or by appointment.

claim: The Georg-Meistermann-Museum (now Städtische Galerie im Alten Rathaus) in Wittlich (~20 km from Piesport) shows the stained-glass and painted works of Wittlich-born modernist Georg Meistermann plus rotating contemporary shows; opens Tue–Sat 11:00–17:00 and Sun/holidays 14:00–17:00, entry €1, key collected at the Altes Rathaus ticket desk on the Marktplatz.
quote: Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm, and Sunday/public holidays 2 pm to 5 pm ... admission is 1 Euro.

claim: Wittlich's Säubrennerkirmes — the town's signature five-day folk festival commemorating the pig-burner legend — runs 14–18 August 2026, with the festive parade and ceremonial roast-pork carving on the Saturday (16 Aug), bands on the Marktplatz and Pariser Platz, and food/wine stands along the festival mile.
quote: Wittlicher Säubrennerkirmes will take place from August 14-18, 2026 ... traditional festival parade with music groups and foot groups through the Wittlich city center, followed by the ceremonial cutting of roasted pork on the market square

claim: Trittenheim's wine-saint chapel (Laurentiuskapelle, on the Laurentiusberg opposite Leiwen, ~10 km from Piesport) was first documented in 1569, restored 1997–1999 and now serves as a war memorial; the village itself has a Trithemius monument, Renaissance baptismal font in the parish church and the only surviving pair of pontoon-ferry towers on the entire Mosel between Perl and Koblenz (in service 1829–1908).
quote: first mentioned in a document in 1569 ... restored exemplarily from 1997 to 1999 by the Förderverein e.V. St. Laurentiuskapelle Trittenheim

claim: Trier sits ~34 km by road (about 25 minutes) southwest of Piesport — outside the 30 km radius — so its UNESCO Roman ensemble (Porta Nigra, Kaiserthermen, Amphitheatre, Konstantinbasilika, Dom) is a half-day trip rather than a 'within-30-km' option; the nearest in-radius Roman monuments are the Mehring villa rustica, the Longuich Villa Urbana, the Piesport Kelteranlage and Neumagen-Dhron's wine-ship and tomb stones.
quote: the road distance between Trier and Piesport is 22 miles (approximately 35 km), and it takes about 25 minutes to drive from Trier to Piesport

claim: Personenschifffahrt Gebr. Kolb runs Mosel cruises in the Bernkastel region from 1 May to 17 Oct 2026 (break 7-17 June) on Tue/Thu/Sat with additional Weds in Aug-Sep; one route is Leiwen-Bernkastel with arrival noon and return at 3pm; adult return 27€ one way 20€.
quote: Schedule runs from 1 May to 6 June and 18 June to 17 October 2026, operating on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays... Adults return trip: 27 €, Adults one way: 20 €, Groups of 10 or more receive 10% discount, and children 6-14 years pay half price.

claim: Personenschifffahrt Gebrüder Kolb is the main operator from Bernkastel-Kues offering one-hour panorama cruises plus longer trips to Traben-Trarbach (2 hours), Alf, and from Leiwen, with themed evening, wine-festival, Advent and BBQ cruises.
quote: Personenschifffahrt Gebrüder Kolb (Gebrüder Kolb Passenger Boat Company) operates the main boat tours from Bernkastel-Kues. Round trips: One-hour panorama cruises departing from Bernkastel. Half-day/day trips: Bernkastel-Kues to Traben-Trarbach (2 hours), Bernkastel-Kues to Alf, Leiwen to Bernkastel-Kues.

claim: Daily Traben-Trarbach to Bernkastel-Kues round-trips run May-October with ~2-hour journey time; adult return 25€, one-way 20€, kids 6-14 half-price, bikes carried on board.
quote: From May to October, several daily scheduled trips operate from Traben-Trarbach to Bernkastel-Kues and back with a journey time of approximately 2 hours... adults return trip for 25€, adults one way for 20€... Bicycles can be taken on board.

claim: Moselradweg Stage 5 (Piesport to Bernkastel-Kues) is 18.5 km along the right bank, mostly flat, passing the Moselloreley rock and wine villages Wintrich, Brauneberg, Mülheim.
quote: The 18.5-kilometre-long cycle tour begins with a view of the natural monument 'Moselloreley', a rock massif rising steeply out of the Moselle. Downstream, the route takes you along vineyards, orchards and picturesque winegrowing villages such as Wintrich, Brauneberg and Mülheim.

claim: Piesport-Bernkastel cycling stage is 18.3 km, ~1h15min easy ride, only 2 m ascent and 16 m descent, altitudes 105-123 m.
quote: Distance: 18.3 km, Duration: 1 hour 15 minutes, Difficulty: Easy, Elevation: Only 2m ascent, 16m descent (ranging from 105m to 123m)

claim: The Moselradweg German section is 248 km from Perl to Koblenz, mostly asphalted and separated from roads, relatively flat, certified as an ADFC 4-star quality cycle route as of 2024.
quote: The German section spans '248 kilometres' from Perl in Saarland to Koblenz... mostly asphalted and run separately from the main roads with relatively flat and without major gradients... ADFC quality cycle route with 4 stars status.

claim: The Bernkastel-Kues holiday region has 13 bike and e-bike borrowing stations, with notable shops including Fun Bike Team (Bernkastel-Kues), Velodocs (Zeltingen-Rachtig), Peter Später (Piesport), and tourist-info-based rentals in Wintrich and Brauneberg.
quote: Fun Bike Team GmbH - Bernkastel-Kues... Bicycle rental Peter Später - Piesport... Tourist Information Brauneberg... The region has '13 borrowing stations' and '7 repair stations' overall.

claim: In Piesport, Fahrradverleih Peter Später (Römerstraße 43, +49 6507 939350) and Altes Kelterhaus (St.-Martin-Straße 33) rent bikes; the Tourist Information has a battery charging station for e-bikes.
quote: Fahrradverleih Peter Später, Römerstraße 43, Tel +49 6507 939 350; Altes Kelterhaus, St.-Martin-Straße 33; Tourist Information Piesport has a battery charging station for electric bikes

claim: Mosel-Kanu-Service in Piesport (Römerstraße 38, +49 6507 5558) rents canoes and kayaks for day or multi-day paddling in the Piesport Mosel loop and Wintrich barrage reservoir; opening times depend on weather.
quote: Location: Piesport, Germany (Römerstraße 38, 54498 Piesport). Phone: +49 6507 5558... The outfit specializes in the Piesport Moselle loop and the Wintrich barrage reservoir area... Opening times vary based on weather conditions.

claim: Mosel-Kanuverleih in Reil (Moselstraße 13, 56861 Reil/Mosel) rents kayaks and canoes from €20, SUP from €10, full-day tours €25-35+, season mid-May through October; life jackets mandatory and included free; multi-day and guided tours available.
quote: Kayaks: From €20; Canoes: From €20; SUP (Stand-Up Paddle): From €10; Full-day tours: €25-€35+; Season: Mid-May through October; 'Wearing a life jacket is mandatory when renting a canoe' and provided free of charge.

claim: Operating Mosel ferries near Trier include the electric Sankta Maria II Oberbillig-Wasserbillig (passengers €1, bikes €1.80, cars €3) and seasonal passenger ferries at Enkirch-Kövenig and Pünderich (€2-2.50, bikes €1.50); historic Wintrich/Köwerich/Brauneberg car ferries no longer run.
quote: Sankta Maria II (electric ferry): Mon-Fri 6:30-13:30; Sat-Sun & holidays 11-17. Prices: Passengers €1, bikes €1.80, cars €3... Enkirch-Kövenig: Easter-end Oct, Wed-Sun... Prices: €2.50 (10+), bikes €1.50

claim: The Burg-Landshut-Express in Bernkastel-Kues is a panoramic shuttle bus (not a chairlift) running every full hour from the Mosel parking lot to the castle ruins, April-October; operator Bustouristik Feuerer (06531-8005).
quote: This is a shuttle/bus service, not a chairlift... Departures: Every full hour from the Mosel parking lot. Seasonal operation: April through October. Bustouristik Feuerer Tel: 06531-8005 or 06531-6144.

claim: Waldkletterpark Wald Abenteuer Leiwen (Sonnenberg 1, 54340 Leiwen) sits in the Landal Sonnenberg resort ~20 min from Trier with adult Adventure ticket €29, under-18 €25, kids' parcours €18; minimum 140cm/11yrs for adult course; online booking with no cancellation fees.
quote: Sonnenberg 1, 54340 Leiwen, Germany. The park is situated within the Landal Sonnenberg holiday resort, approximately 20 minutes from Trier. Kinder-Parcours: €18.00; Adventure-Parcours (under 18): €25.00; Adventure-Parcours (18+): €29.00.

claim: Moseltherme is located at Wildsteiner Weg 5, 56841 Traben-Trarbach (~30 km from Piesport), spans over 2,000 m² with thermal pool (32°C), multi-purpose pool, outdoor pool plus sauna landscape (steam bath, Finnish, salt room).
quote: Wildsteiner Weg 5, 56841 Traben-Trarbach ... Thermal bath (140m², 32°C) with whirlpool ... Multi-purpose pool (210m², 28°C) ... Outdoor pool (140m², 32°C) ... Steam bath, bio-sauna, Finnish sauna, salt room

claim: Moseltherme bath area hours: Mon 14:00–21:00, Tue–Fri 9:00–21:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 9:00–18:00; adult bath ticket €4 for 1 hr, €7.50 for 3 hrs; full-day sauna+bath €17 for adults 16+.
quote: Monday 14:00-21:00, Tuesday-Friday 9:00-21:00, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays 9:00-18:00 ... €4.00 for 1 hour, €6.00 for 2 hours, or €7.50 for 3 hours ... daily ticket for sauna and swimming costs €17.00 for adults 16+

claim: Vulkaneifel Therme at Clara-Viebig-Str. 3-7, 56864 Bad Bertrich (~30 km via the Eifel) opens daily 9:00–22:00 for the thermal bath; sauna Mon–Thu 11–22, Fri–Sun 9–22; closed for maintenance 15–28 June 2026.
quote: Clara-Viebig-Straße 3-7, 56864 Bad Bertrich ... täglich 9.00 – 22.00 Uhr ... The facility will be closed June 15–28, 2026 for annual maintenance

claim: Vulkaneifel Therme thermal-only pricing: 2 hrs €11, 3 hrs €12.50, day ticket €15.50; thermal + sauna combined €20 for 2 hrs and €25 day ticket.

claim: Vinothek im Cusanusstift offers over 160 Mosel wines and Sekt; tasting flight of 120-160 wines costs €15; admission without tasting is free.
quote: 120 und 160 Weine zwischen QbA und Auslese ... 15 euros ... A visit to the vinothek without wine tasting is free of charge

claim: Library tours of the Cusanusstift (St. Nikolaus-Hospital) showing Nikolaus von Kues' 15th-century manuscript collection run only Tuesdays at 10:30 and Fridays at 15:00, April–October.
quote: Tuesday: 10:30 a.m. ... Friday: 3:00 p.m. ... provides information about the historic building and its furnishings, the founder Nikolaus von Kues and his world-famous library

claim: The Cusanusstift library holds about 314 manuscripts and 132 incunabula and is one of the most valuable private medieval manuscript collections in Europe, viewable only via guided tour.
quote: impressive collection of 314 manuscripts, predominantly in Latin ... 132 incunabula, early printed books dating back to the 15th century ... only be viewed as part of a guided tour

claim: The Historisches Spielzeug- und Ikonenmuseum at Kloster Machern (An der Zeltinger Brücke, 54470 Bernkastel-Kues, ~20 km from Piesport) opens Tue–Sun 10:30–17:30; adults €4, children €2, family €11.
quote: An der Zeltinger Brücke, 54470 Bernkastel-Kues ... dienstags bis sonntags: 10:30 – 17:30 Uhr ... Adults: €4.00 - Children (8-17 years): €2.00 - Family card (parents + up to 3 children): €11.00

claim: The Kloster Machern complex opposite Zeltingen-Rachtig houses a working monastery brewery (Klosterbrauerei founded 2004), wine cellar and bistro serving in-house brewed beer alongside top regional wines, with Moselle and vineyard views.
quote: former Cistercian monastery opposite the village of Zeltingen-Rachtig ... monastery brewery ... cold beer brewed in-house by master brewer Michael Berthold ... wines from top regional wineries

claim: Brennerei Hubertus Vallendar in Kail (Eifel side, ~30 km from Piesport) is a Bauhaus-style premium distillery producing ~80,000 bottles/year and twice named World-Class Distillery at the 2026 World Spirits Award; tastings for groups of 10+.
quote: state-of-the-art Bauhaus-style distillery is located in Kail on the Moselle ... 80,000 bottles leave the manufactory per year ... World Spirits Award 2026, Brennerei Vallendar was awarded World-Class Distillery designation twice

claim: Weingut & Brennerei Hans Beth in Kröv (~22 km from Piesport) has distilled Mosel Edelbrände since 1991; their shop at Moselweinstraße 58 opens daily in season 10:00–18:00 for tastings of fruit brandies, Mosel Gin and Riesling Mustard.
quote: Berghof 3 in Kröv ... wine shop is at Moselweinstraße 58 ... open daily during the season from 10:00 to 18:00 for small tastings ... Mosel premium spirits ... since 1991

claim: Hunsrückhaus at Erbeskopf (highest point in Rheinland-Pfalz, ~30 km south of Piesport) serves as the National Park Hunsrück-Hochwald gateway with a free interactive indoor/outdoor exhibition, ranger meeting point and bistro, open daily 9:00–17:00.
quote: National Park indoor and outdoor exhibition is interactive and multimedia ... Admission is free ... National Park gateway and exhibition are open Monday through Sunday from 9 to 5 PM

claim: The Elfengrotte (a.k.a. Käsegrotte, sometimes called the Romantikgrotte) at the western edge of Bad Bertrich is a basalt-lava cave with cheese-wheel column formations and a small waterfall, reached via a 2.4 km easy walking trail.
quote: Elfengrotte is an impressive natural monument ... also called the Käsegrotte ... basalt lava flow shows columnar formations ... 2.4 km walking trail ... waterfall cascades over the cooled lava flow

claim: Hallenbad Vitelliusbad in Wittlich (~22 km from Piesport) opens Mon 7:00–15:00, Tue 7:00–21:30 (warm-water 30°C day), Wed 7:00–18:30+, Thu 7:00–18:30, Fri 7:00–17:00 & 19:00–21:30, Sat split sessions, Sun/holidays 8:00–16:00; indoor pool closes during outdoor season.
quote: Monday: 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM ... Tuesday (warm water day at 30°C): 7:00 AM to 9:30 PM ... Sundays and public holidays: 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM ... During the outdoor pool season, the indoor pool is closed

claim: Moselbad indoor pool in Bernkastel-Kues at Peter-Kremer-Weg 5 opens Mon–Fri 8:00–19:00 and Sat/Sun/holidays 9:00–19:00 with sports pool, warm whirlpool and baby splash area; adults €6, children €3.50; indoor season ends 30 April 2026.
quote: Monday to Friday: 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM ... Saturday/Sunday & holidays: 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM ... Adults: €6.00; Children: €3.50 ... indoor pool season ends on Thursday, April 30, 2026

claim: Moselschlösschen Spa & Resort in Traben-Trarbach (~30 km) offers a day-spa ticket: all-day wellness access 8:00–20:00 for €98 pp, or €195 pp with breakfast; 2,500 m² wellness area with infinity pool, six saunas and fitness/yoga studio.
quote: all-day stay in the wellness area from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. for €98 per person ... €195 per person ... 2,500 m² and features numerous saunas, relaxation rooms, fitness and yoga studio as well as an infinity pool

claim: Escape Room Mosel in Traben-Trarbach (~30 km from Piesport) runs custom-designed escape scenarios on a 440 m² play area within a 10,000 m² site, with on-site dining rooms; players are not actually locked in.
quote: 10,000 square meter property includes 440 square meters of play area plus dining rooms ... In all our game rooms, you will not be locked in at any time

claim: Mittelmosel-Museum in baroque Villa Böcking, Casinostraße 2, 56841 Traben-Trarbach opens Tue–Fri 10–17 and Sat/Sun 12–16 from 2 April to 1 November 2026; closed Mondays and during winter break.
quote: Tuesday to Friday: 10 – 17 o'clock; Saturday and Sunday: 12 – 16 o'clock ... Casinostraße 2, 56841 Traben-Trarbach ... closed until April 1, 2026 due to winter break

claim: Indoor museums in Wittlich include the Städtische Galerie im Alten Rathaus (Georg Meistermann modern-art collection) and CASA Tony M. in the restored 1750s Baroque Alte Posthalterei Thurn & Taxis showing rotating Tony Munzlinger exhibitions.
quote: Städtische Galerie für Moderne Kunst im Alten Rathaus ... permanent exhibitions of artistic works by Georg Meistermann ... CASA Tony M. is housed in the Alte Posthalterei Thurn & Taxis, a magnificent Baroque building from the 1750s

claim: Weinfest der Mittelmosel in Bernkastel-Kues runs September 3-7, 2026, with Saturday fireworks, Sunday parade, Thursday Moselblümchen evening, and a wine route featuring 20+ Mosel communities.
quote: The festival runs September 3-7, 2026 in Bernkastel-Kues, Germany. Over 20 Moselle communities showcase high-quality range of Riesling and other types of wine across a 300-meter stretch with food stalls and live music.

claim: Bernkastel-Kues is a medieval twin town on the Mosel famous for its half-timbered Marktplatz, the 1416 Spitzhäuschen (Pointed House), the 1608 Renaissance Town Hall and the world-class Doctor vineyard.
quote: The famous Spitzhäuschen (Pointed House), built in 1416, is a half-timbered, pointed-roof building among the oldest structures in Bernkastel. The 400-year-old half-timbered houses, the Renaissance town hall from the year 1608...

claim: Traben-Trarbach is celebrated for its Art Nouveau (Jugendstil) architecture introduced by Berlin architect Bruno Möhring around 1900, including the iconic Bridge Gate, Villa Nollen, and the Buddha-Museum in the former Kayser winery.
quote: Berlin architect Bruno Möhring introduced Art Nouveau to Traben-Trarbach around 1900, having been commissioned to build a new bridge over the Mosel River. The iconic Traben-Trarbach Bridge Gate is an Art Nouveau masterpiece by Bruno Möhring.

claim: Traben-Trarbach was the second-largest wine-trading hub in Europe in the late 19th century, leaving a legacy of grand Art Nouveau villas and extensive underground wine cellars open for tours.
quote: the second-biggest wine-trading place in Europe in the second half of the 19th century... magnificent big art nouveau villas and extensive underground wine cellars that remain defining features.

claim: The Mosel-Wein-Nachts-Markt in Traben-Trarbach is staged inside historic underground wine cellars and runs November 20, 2026 - January 2, 2027 (Fri-Sun) with extended daily hours over the holidays.
quote: The underground Christmas market runs from November 20, 2026 to January 2, 2027 on weekends. The market is open Friday-Sunday 11 AM to 9 PM from November 20-December 28, 2026.

claim: Trittenheim sits on a tight Moselschleife hairpin loop just upstream of Piesport, famed for the Riesling Grosse Lagen Apotheke and Altärchen, the 16th-century Laurentius chapel above the vines, and the prehistoric Hinkelstein megalith.
quote: Trittenheim is a village in the Mosel wine region of Germany, principally known for white wines from the Riesling grape. The best known vineyards are Trittenheimer Apotheke and Trittenheimer Altärchen... In the vineyards above the village are the Laurentius chapel from the 16th century and the famous Hinkelstein Eselstratt.

claim: Zeltingen-Rachtig, between Bernkastel-Kues and Traben-Trarbach, is one of the Middle Mosel's largest wine-growing communes (133 ha) with the Grosse Lage Zeltinger Sonnenuhr, a southwest-facing blue Devonian slate slope marked by a historic sundial.
quote: With 133 ha of vineyards, the double municipality is among the biggest winegrowing centres on the Middle Moselle... Zeltingen's sole Grosse Lage site is its portion of the acclaimed Sonnenuhr (Sundial) vineyard... It is a southwest-facing slope of blue Devonian slate.

claim: Ürzig has the highest share of steep vineyards of any German wine town; its Ürziger Würzgarten grows on red volcanic slate and the village preserves a half-timbered Rathausplatz and the oldest sundial in the Mosel valley.
quote: Ürzig boasts the highest percentage of steep vineyards of any winegrowing town in Germany... Ürziger Würzgarten, or 'spice garden of Ürzig,' is one of the most distinctive sites in Germany, with red volcanic slate that yields explosively aromatic and exotic wines.

claim: Brauneberg, downstream of Piesport, is defined by the Brauneberger Juffer Grosse Lage on some of Germany's warmest slopes, a 2.2 km walnut-tree avenue along the Mosel, the leaning tower of St. Remigius and a reconstructed 2nd-century Roman wine press.
quote: Brauneberg is famous for its exceptional wines, particularly the renowned 'Brauneberger Juffer' vineyard. The region experiences 'some of the warmest temperatures in Germany'... A distinctive 2,200-meter-long tree-lined promenade (Nussbaumallee) runs through the town.

claim: Mülheim is the gateway to the ruined 12th-century Schloss Veldenz, the former largest castle of the Central Moselle, razed by Louis XIV; guided tours run Wednesdays 3 PM April-October and a working trebuchet is on site.
quote: Veldenz Castle is one of the biggest castles on the Moselle from the 12th century, situated about 5 km from wine-growing village Mülheim... Interesting tours of the castle and its exciting history take place regularly every Wednesday at 3:00 PM from April to October.

claim: Wittlich's historic Marktplatz is the cultural heart of the Eifel-edge town, surrounded by the 1652 Renaissance Old Town Hall (now the city gallery with Georg Meistermann works), the Baroque Church of St. Markus and Renaissance and Baroque townhouses.
quote: The Old Town Hall, which was built in 1652 in renaissance style, now houses the city gallery of art and the cultural office. The exhibition on the ground floor is dedicated to the well-known artist Georg Meistermann.

claim: Trittenheim lies a short upstream ride from Piesport along the Mosel and shares the Piesporter Michelsberg appellation, with its vineyards wrapping the famous Moselschleife river bend.
quote: Trittenheim is located upstream from Piesport on a southeast-oriented slope on a hairpin bend in the Mosel river... The wine village of Trittenheim sits in the middle of an incredibly spectacular and very famous tight loop in the Mosel River, called a 'Moselschleife'.
